newsitem.title: UK: European VGO firmer with some buying interest.
newsitem.headline: European VGO firmer with some buying interest.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil ended the week a shade firmer with some buying interest coming into the market, and traders said that the arbitrage to the U.S. was marginally open.
Traders said the market firmed from mid-week but added that no fresh deals were reported after a low sulphur VGO cargo was traded on Wednesday at a floating price.
"(Low sulphur) VGO is a little firmer but there's not a lot of liquidity in the market...But at least there are buyers, so demand is better, last week it was low," a trader said.
There was talk of two players looking to buy in the U.K market and may be others into Norway. Offers were around the $123 mark on a delivered basis, trades said.
The arbitrage to the U.S., said to be shut in mid-week, was now marginally open.
The netback for moving low sulphur VGO to the U.S. improved to about $115 per tonne, or $5 up on mid-week.
"The arb is marginally open with mogas and heating oil rising," a trader said.
Traders said crude's rise gave support to VGO.
"With crude rising VGO becomes cheap as feedstock and people get more interested in it," a trader said.
